subject.title: [Feature Request]: Native Prompt Caching Support for Amazon Nova (Bedrock)

question: Should OpenClaw change direct Amazon Bedrock Nova models from forced no-cache to native cache-point eligible behavior once redacted live Nova proof is available?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the change alters provider request shaping, cache defaults, and billing/performance behavior for existing Nova users, and it still depends on current AWS Bedrock live-contract proof.

options.title: Land after live Nova proof
options.body: Require redacted Converse or ConverseStream proof showing accepted cachePoint payloads and cache read/write accounting, then land the linked PR or an equivalent narrow provider-owned fix.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in first
options.body: Preserve no-cache as the upgrade default and allow Nova cache points only through an explicit user setting or narrower policy gate.

options.title: Defer Nova native caching
options.body: Leave the existing forced no-cache behavior in place until maintainers have stronger live provider proof or a clearer AWS/provider contract signal.

recommendation.title: Land after live Nova proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted Converse or ConverseStream proof showing accepted cachePoint payloads and cache read/write accounting, then land the linked PR or an equivalent narrow provider-owned fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and Bedrock cache-path history make this the strongest available routing signal for the provider behavior decision.
